diagnostics.message: google_organization_iam_binding.authoritative can grant roles supplied in var.iam, including custom roles just created by google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles in this same module. Newly created custom roles are eventually consistent and may not be usable in an IAM policy write immediately, so without a dependency the binding can fail with "role does not exist". The source explicitly notes this ordering is "left to the caller", and currently there is neither an implicit reference nor a depends_on expressing it.

google_organization_iam_binding.bindings takes arbitrary role strings from var.iam_bindings, which may name custom roles created by google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles in this module. Because custom roles are eventually consistent after creation, the binding should be ordered after the role exists; right now no attribute reference or depends_on establishes this ordering.

google_organization_iam_member.bindings takes arbitrary role strings from var.iam_bindings_additive, which may name custom roles created by google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles in this module. Newly created custom roles are eventually consistent, so the member binding should depend on role creation; currently nothing in the graph expresses that ordering.
